findings.title: Reschedules bypass deferred cancellation and retry handling
findings.body: The reschedule path calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` with `immediateDelete=true`, so it posts the cancellation to SendGrid immediately instead of marking the reminder `cancelled` for the cron. SendGrid keeps pending cancellations until their scheduled dates, which can again exhaust the 100-cancellation limit. Also, if this request fails, the helper only logs the error and never sets `cancelled`, so the cron will not retry and the old reminder can still be sent.

findings.title: The cancellation cron can still exceed SendGrid's 100-cancellation limit
findings.body: The one-hour window does not cap how many cancellations this loop submits. If more than 100 cancelled reminders are due within that window, SendGrid can reject requests after the limit; the surrounding catch then stops processing the remaining reminders. Those reminders remain scheduled and can be sent before a later cron run retries them. The cron needs to defer or otherwise limit requests so it does not exceed the pending-cancellation cap.
